proofUses.reason: Differentiate the progeny generating equation at positive field, normalize the finite-progeny expectation, and apply Laplace-transform convergence.
Apply the fixed-scale size-bias transfer to the finite-progeny law and keep the survival atom separate.
The marked-tree product weights realize the consistent size-biased restrictions; extinction of the countably many ordinary grafts gives a unique infinite ray.
The branching conditional density is dominated by the spine density up to a scalar. A mixture decomposition bounds total variation, and the survival ratio tends to one for r=o(R).
Uniform integrability permits biasing the Yaglom limit. The branching survival weight gives comparable-horizon laws; total variation transfers the spine limit when the horizon is much farther away.
Size bias inserts one marked vertex; finite moment-measure convergence gives spatial tightness and the exponential total-mass bound gives uniqueness.
Gamma duplication identifies the mixed edge lengths; the unit-mass CRT reduced-tree law and construction of its spatial motion remain explicit cited inputs.
Condition on the lower cluster and use the last exit to a ghost-marked vertex; the outside product law and added-edge row bound control the discrepancy.
A truncated-tail integral and fixed-multiplier regular variation make the omitted mass negligible at the rare-event normalization.
Bounded-Lipschitz tests transfer finite weighted laws; upper-tail control and absence of a threshold atom justify conditioning.
Undo size bias away from zero mass, retain the scale factors, and change all tree coordinates to identify the rescaled-kernel diagrams.
Weight first by a compact local mass to obtain finite measures; factorial moments identify that limit, and spatial tightness then replaces local mass by total mass.
